candidates.name: Frauenkirche
candidates.content: The original Church of Our Lady was completely destroyed during World War II; however, it has been reconstructed. The City of Coventry, which was raided by the Luftwaffe in WWII, donated the golden cross for the dome of the church

candidates.name: Zwinger Palace
candidates.price: Entry is free to the palace, but to see exhibitions you need a ticket. Combined ticket for all three exhibitions: adults pre-booking , reduced , under 7 free
candidates.content: The baroque palace features a nympheum, many sculptures of Permoser, a bell pavilion and famous art collections. Do not miss the "Alte Meister" - you'll find Rafael's famous Sistine Madonna with its well-known angels there. Three

candidates.name: Residenzschloss
candidates.content: During the bombing of Dresden in February 1945 the interior of the palace was almost completely destroyed by fire. Only the part that is now the Historisches Grünes Gewölbe (and the basements) was unaffected. Due to lack of money

candidates.name: Grünes Gewölbe
candidates.price: €18, including Audioguide, concessions €13.50, children <16: free. Tickets for the Historisches Grünes Gewölbe have a clearly defined time limit
candidates.hours: Wed Thu Sat Sun 10:00-17:00, Fri 10:00-19:00 closed Tuesdays
candidates.content: One of the most significant collections of European goldsmith's work and decorative arts. The museum is divided into two sections, each requiring a separate ticket. The Historic Green Vault (Historisches Grünes Gewölbe) preserves

candidates.name: Kupferstich-Kabinett
candidates.alt: Collection of Prints, Drawings and Photographs
candidates.content: One of the world’s oldest and most significant museums specializing in drawings, prints, and photographs. The collection spans from the Middle Ages to the present day, featuring works by renowned masters such as Albrecht Dürer, Re

candidates.name: Dreikönigskirche
candidates.price: For the tower: adults €5, reduced €4, children €6-17 €1.50, under 10 free
candidates.hours: For the tower: Mar-Oct: Tue 11:30-16:00, Wed-Sat 11:00-17:00, Sun and holidays 11:30-17:00, Mon closed. Nov-Feb: Wed 12:00-16:00, Thu-Sat 10:00-16:00, Sun and holidays 11:30-16:30, Mon Tue closed. Last admission 30min before closing
candidates.content: You get a nice view of the whole city and the price of admission to climb the tower is lower than at the more famous Frauenkirche. There are also some nice pieces in the church that were not destroyed in the World War II bombings,

candidates.name: Schloß Pillnitz
candidates.price: There are no entry fees, although there still is a debate about a small fee
candidates.content: Pillnitz is the old garden residence of the Saxon kings, built at the end of the 18th century in a Japanese but also English style outside of what was then-Dresden, as the closest out-of-town residence of the kings. Pillnitz was t

candidates.name: Albertinum Museum
candidates.content: The "New Masters" collections feature a wonderful range from romantic painters like Caspar David Friedrich to Rotloff and Van Gogh. The Albertinum is part of the Dresden State Art Collections (SKD).

candidates.sec: Part of Museen der Stadt Dresden
candidates.name: Carl-Maria-von-Weber-Museum
candidates.price: Adults €4, reduced €3. Free entry every Friday from 13:00 (except on holidays)
candidates.content: Closed for renovations until 2028Dedicated to Dresden's most famous composer. Part of the Dresden City Museum. An additional webpage describes the museum in English.

candidates.sec: Part of Museen der Stadt Dresden
candidates.name: Kunsthaus Dresden
candidates.content: An exhibition hall for contemporary art. They also hold concerts, lectures, workshops and show movies. This additional webpage also describes the museum.

candidates.sec: Part of Museen der Stadt Dresden
candidates.name: Leonhardi Museum
candidates.price: Adults €6, reduced €4, under 7 free. Free entry Fridays from 2pm (except on holidays)
candidates.content: The building was used as a studio and museum by the artist Eduard Leonhardi (late Romanticism) until he died in 1905. From 1963 to 1990, contemporary art exhibitions showing works from progressive GDR artists were held despite man

candidates.sec: Part of Museen der Stadt Dresden
candidates.name: Dresden City Art Museum
candidates.price: Adults €5, reduced €4, under 7 free. Free entry every Friday from 12:00 (except on holidays). A combination ticket with the Dresden City Museum is available
candidates.hours: Tue-Thu Sat Sun and holidays 10:00-18:00, Fri 10:00-19:00, Mon closed
candidates.content: Art from Dresden and the region with a main focus on the 20th century to the present. The collection also contains pieces of art dating back until the 16th century. Originally the collection was part of the Dresden City Museum in

candidates.name: Erich-Kästner-Museum
candidates.hours: Sun-Wed Fri 10:00-18:00, Tue and Sat closed
candidates.content: Dedicated to author, poet, screenwriter and satirist Emil Erich Kästner, known primarily for his humorous, socially astute poetry and children's literature such as Emil and the Detectives who was born and grew up in Dresden.

candidates.name: Military History Museum
candidates.hours: Mon 10:00-21:00, Tue Thu-Sun 10:00-18:00, last tickets sold at 17:00
candidates.content: Exhibits relating to Germany's military history - and the country's complicated relationship with its armed forces and warfare. 20,000 m² of indoor and outdoor exhibition space and a collection of 1.2 million exhibits.

candidates.name: German Hygiene Museum
candidates.hours: Tue-Sun and holidays 10:00-17:00, Mon closed. Last admission 30 min before closing
candidates.content: A comprehensive museum dedicated to "science, culture and society", a truly vast scope including all aspects of the human body, sickness, health, stages of life and sexuality. Don't be put off by the old-fashioned name. The childr

candidates.name: Fürstenzug
candidates.content: This biggest porcelain painting of the world shows (almost) all Saxon princes, electors and kings on their horses and splendid parade uniforms. (There is only one female person at the painting, find her.) It leads to the "Stallhof

candidates.name: Kulturpalast
candidates.content: A socialist era building finished in 1969, standing right in the middle of the gradually reconstructed Altstadt, in stark contrast to the historic buildings surrounding it and supplanting some of the old buildings that closed the

candidates.name: Schloss Albrechtsberg
candidates.content: The neoclassical castle above the Elbe river in Dresden's Loschwitz district was erected in 1854 and can be viewed best from the south side of the Elbe river.

candidates.name: Lingnerschloss
candidates.content: The castle above the Elbe River was built from 1850 tom 1853 by Prince Albert of Prussia. The castle houses a restaurant and an outdoor terrace with beer garden that offers a fantastic view over the Elbe River and Dresden.

candidates.name: Gohliser Windmühle
candidates.content: This beautiful old windmill was built in 1828 and is now a museum and tavern. It includes a beer garden; best reached using Elberadweg cycle route south of the Elbe river.

candidates.name: Japanisches Palais
candidates.content: The palace was bombed out and in its partially restored state houses several small museums, including a museum of natural history of the region and a display of assorted exotic garments (ethnological collection). The palace is par

candidates.sec: Part of Museen der Stadt Dresden
candidates.name: Dresden City Museum
candidates.price: Adults €5, reduced €4, under 7 free. Free entry every Friday from 12:00 (except on holidays). A combination ticket with the Dresden City Art Museum is available
candidates.hours: Tue-Thu Sat Sun and holidays 10:00-18:00, Fri 10:00-19:00, Mon closed
candidates.content: An additional webpage describes the museum in English.

candidates.name: Dresden Transport Museum
candidates.content: The museum is housed in the Johanneum at the Neumarkt, near Frauenkirche.

candidates.name: Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister
candidates.price: Entrance only with the combined ticket
candidates.content: A highly regarded collection featuring around 700 European works from the 15th to the 18th century. It is particularly known for its focus on Italian Renaissance and Baroque art, including Raphael's Sistine Madonna, as well as a s

candidates.name: Porzellansammlung
candidates.price: Individual tickets: adults €6, reduced €4.50, under 17 free
candidates.content: A unique collection showcasing the obsession with "white gold" during the 18th century. It features thousands of exquisite pieces from China, Japan, and the first European porcelain factory in Meißen, founded by Augustus the Stron

candidates.name: Mathematisch-Physikalischer Salon
candidates.alt: Royal Cabinet of Mathematical and Physical Instruments
candidates.price: Individual tickets: adults €6, reduced €4.50, under 17 free
candidates.content: A collection of historical scientific instruments from the 18th century. It features a variety of early precision tools, including telescopes, clocks, and celestial models that reflect the scientific interests and technological ad

candidates.name: Semperoper
candidates.alt: Saxon State Opera and concert hall
candidates.price: Guided tours: adults €16, photo fee per person €3. Entry fee varies for each performance
candidates.hours: Guided tours in English daily 13:00 and 14:00, frequent tours in German
candidates.content: This opera house is known for its architecture and the Staatskapelle Dresden orchestra. Its history includes the premieres of several operas by Wagner and Strauss. Tickets should be booked in advance, though some last-minute ticke

candidates.name: Neue Synagoge
candidates.content: The New Synagogue is on the site of what was the Semper Synagogue. The old one was designed by Gottfried Semper, who also designed the Semper Opera in Dresden. Erected in 1840 and destroyed by the Nazis in the pogroms of November

candidates.name: Theaterruine St. Pauli
candidates.content: This ruin of a former Lutheran church that was bombed out in World War II is used as a theatre and concert venue nowadays and represents the cultural centre of the Hechtviertel district.

candidates.name: Dresden Monarchs
candidates.content: American Football - German Football League. Founded in 1992 they are the only "true eastern" (i.e. apart from Berlin) American Football team to play in the first division. A first division team since 2002 they have made the playof

candidates.name: Dynamo Dresden
candidates.content: One of the best soccer teams of what was East Germany, they have been struggling on and off the field. They were relegated in 2020 and now play soccer in the Second Liga, but are still fervently loved by their fans who have a sort

candidates.name: Elberadweg
candidates.content: Do a bicycling tour on this popular cycle route along the Elbe river that offers spectacular views. The Elberadweg is a 1220-km-long cycleway, and within Dresden it follows the Elbe river on both sides from the very southeast to N

candidates.name: Dixieland Festival
candidates.content: Europe's biggest jazz festival. It normally takes place in the second week of May and attracts bands and visitors from all over Europe, America and the rest of the world. A great deal of the music is played on the top decks of pad

candidates.name: Bunte Republik Neustadt (BRN)
candidates.content: A massive yearly street festival that consumes the Neustadt part of Dresden in June. The festival consists of many stages featuring local musicians of different styles. The festivities run very late into the night with plenty of b

candidates.name: Filmnächte
candidates.content: A huge movie screen offers cinema (in German) in a beautiful setting and there are also many concerts with popular stars. Again, it is the biggest event of its kind in Europe!

candidates.name: Ostrale
candidates.content: One of Germany's biggest expositions of contemporary art, the Ostrale was begun in 2007 on the Ostragehege, a former abattoir. The area is located on a peninsula created by the river Elbe, and is in the heart of the former world h

candidates.name: Striezelmarkt
candidates.hours: From the end of November until Christmas
candidates.content: One of Germany's oldest Christmas Markets. Located at the Altmarkt, all kinds of stalls selling among other things mulled wine (Glühwein) - delicious! Expect to pay a deposit for the mug/glass. Expect crowded streets and traffic j

candidates.name: KlangNetz-Dresden
candidates.content: A network of orchestras, musicians and ensembles organizing concerts with a focus on new music.

candidates.name: Paddle-Steamer Tour
candidates.content: Best start your tour from the main pier at the castle and go down to Meissen or up to Pillnitz or Saxon Switzerland.

candidates.name: Sächsische Staatskapelle Dresden
candidates.content: Referred to colloquially as the Staatskapelle Dresden, it is one of the oldest orchestras in the world, founded in 1548. Its home venue is the Semperoper. The principal conductor is Daniele Gatti.

candidates.name: Stauseebad Cossebaude
candidates.content: On hot summer days, go swimming or windsurfing at this public bathing pool at the Stausee Niederwartha reservoir. Also includes a long waterslide and beach volleyball courts.

candidates.name: Dresden Night of Museums
candidates.hours: At the end of June/beginning of July
candidates.content: An annual event opening many museums for one night (between 18:00 and 24:00). The ticket gives access to all participating museums, and provides free public transport.

candidates.name: Dresden Philharmonic
candidates.content: Orchestra founded in 1870. Their main venue is in the Kulturpalast, the principal conductor is Donald Runnicles.

candidates.name: Ice skating at the JoyNext Arena
candidates.content: Indoor and outdoor, daily from the end of October to beginning of March. Skate rental available. "Ice Disco" with a DJ on Saturday evenings.

candidates.name: Canaletto Dresden Stadtfest
candidates.content: This very well organized 3-day festival encompasses much of the Innere Altstadt and parts of Neustadt. There are hundreds of food and drink booths, representing a very wide variety of German and international cuisine from 6 contin

candidates.name: Hechtfest
candidates.content: This annual three-day alternative street festival in Dresden's trendy Hechtviertel district offers dozens of street and backyard concerts, street raves, food stands, flea market, art and interactive performances, and attracts thou

candidates.name: Audio tour: Jewish life in Dresden 1933-1945
candidates.content: Download the free map and audio tracks (in English) and take yourself on a walk covering the history of Jewish life in Dresden from 1933 to 1945. You will need several hours.

candidates.name: Hochschule für Musik Carl Maria von Weber Dresden
candidates.content: The music conservatoire hosts regular concerts and events at various venues.

candidates.name: Kraftwerk Mitte
candidates.content: One of Dresden's largest nightclubs, hosting parties, raves, concerts and festivals in a former coal-fired power plant.

candidates.name: Bar Peanuts
candidates.content: Small, cozy bar is located at the corner of the Hilton overlooking the Elbe. Peanut shells are scattered on the floor and as the name suggests, peanuts are the central theme. Cocktails and beer are the main draws here, along with

candidates.name: Riesa efau
candidates.content: The pub is managed by a local events group and features a wide selection of drinks along with a regular slate of activities and entertainment. Good menu of regional beers and mixed drinks, as well as non-alcoholic drinks and coffe

candidates.name: Alter Schlachthof
candidates.content: Popular concert venue in an old slaughterhouse building from the 19th century.

candidates.name: Blue Note
candidates.content: This is the Dresden Jazz point. In the web page you may find the schedule of concerts. There is always very good music. This is a place to sit and enjoy good music. The scotch bar has very good drinks to enjoy during the concert.

candidates.name: Café Europa
candidates.content: This pleasant café and bar is a great choice for a pre-dinner cocktail or late-night snack. The café closes only one hour a day, so stop by any time. In addition to great drinks, the menu also features a full breakfast menu, which

candidates.name: Downtown
candidates.content: The most popular club in the Neustadt. They play mostly mainstream/top 40/1980s music. If this place isn't your scene, you can always go upstairs to Groove Station.

candidates.name: Hebeda's
candidates.content: This pub is quite popular with locals, especially on Friday and Saturday nights. The old East German furniture gives it a cozy and retro feel. Beer is cheap and there's a small dance floor for those who feel like dancing.

candidates.name: Katy's Garage
candidates.content: If you're walking around Neustadt, you can't miss the beer garden at Katy's Garage. It's a great place to have a drink when it's warm outside. When the beer garden closes at around 22:00, you can make your way into their night clu

candidates.name: Louisengarten
candidates.content: Located a few meters from Katy's Garage, this beer garden is only open when it's warm outside. You can come here and relax with a Lenin's Hanf, a delicious beer brewed in the Neustadt.

candidates.name: Ost-Pol
candidates.content: Ost-Pol (translation: East-Pole) is a bar with a retro East German feel to it. They often have live bands, but the place is still good to go for a beer when there's no live music. The beer is pretty cheap, and is one of the few pl

candidates.name: Sektor Evolution
candidates.content: Club in the northern industrial area of Dresden, focusing on techno, house and psytrance parties, but also staging art and theater events. Many guests use drugs.

candidates.name: Studiobar
candidates.content: The best cocktails in town are available here. Located on the 2nd floor, it is a little bit hard to find. From the entrance, go into the main floor bar and straight to the back. There is a staircase that leads up to the second flo

candidates.name: Wohnzimmer Dresden
candidates.content: This cozy retro café and bar right at Alaunstraße, which is fitted out with vintage furniture, offers cocktails and cake and on Sundays from 17:00 live concerts from indie to electronica.

candidates.name: Volkshaus Laubegast
candidates.content: A simple local eatery and café right on the river. The food tends to be stereotypically German (schnitzel, sausages, and the like) and is generally good. Their fried potatoes are excellent, though their green vegetables are overco

candidates.name: Cafe Toscana
candidates.content: A pleasant café with a pastry shop (Konditorei) and a restaurant. The cakes are gorgeous and will help you understand why the café is famous. The décor is fairly new, given the very long history of the place (it was named after Lo

candidates.name: Ballhaus Watzke
candidates.content: Late 19th century brewery, ballroom, restaurant and beer garden with a nice view over the Elbe river.

candidates.name: Brauhaus am Waldschlößchen
candidates.content: Traditional German cuisine with a taste of beer brewed on site. Located on a hill with a splendid view over Elbe riverside from the garden. The food is recommended if you want to experience what German cuisine should taste like.

candidates.name: Hot Shüzzle
candidates.content: Real Thai street food. With a chef from Thailand, Hot Shüzzle has the most authentic Thai food in Dresden.

candidates.name: SchillerGarten
candidates.content: Reservations recommended. Yes, all the tour buses pull up here, but that doesn't stop the locals from heading to SchillerGarten either. A good selection of German cuisines, including an excellent schnitzel. In the summer, there is

candidates.name: Vita Life Soup & Sushi
candidates.content: Try traditional Vietnamese pho. Good, freshly prepared food. Simply authentic.

candidates.name: Pizza 5
candidates.content: At the "entrance" of Neustadt, this pizza place may not look like much, but the pies (30 cm) are good value for the money. Also try the "Pizzabrötchen", small rolls filled with various ingredients. They offer call for pickup but n

candidates.name: Mamma Mia
candidates.content: Italian food with locally made pasta.

candidates.name: Zum Schießhaus
candidates.content: This farmhouse-restaurant is not so easy to find. It lies behind the "Herzogin Garten" (which is a ruin) and behind the opera-house. The large Biergarden is a very relaxing place, has good food and good prices and is very pleasant

candidates.name: Vecchia Napoli
candidates.content: A good Italian restaurant, with a wood fired pizza oven. You can get a pizza or pasta, or a full multicourse meal. Generally very busy, and the food is excellent.

candidates.name: Curry24
candidates.content: Delicious fries, delicious curry sausage, friendly service and with a pleasant Dresden dialect. Also great for Frankfurter and Krakauer sausages. Plus Saxon charm.

candidates.name: Neustädter Markthalle
candidates.hours: Mon-Sat 08:00-20:00, closed on Sundays. Opening hours of individual stalls varies
candidates.content: A market hall.

december.text: Math Adventure Land (website in German). An entertaining hands-on exhibition on mathematics. Suitable for all ages, multilingual. Open Tuesdays to Sundays in the Technology Museum, Junghansstr. 1-3.

Dresden is particularly famous for its Stollen (a Christmas cake made from yeast dough with raisins, butter and almonds) Locals perennially discuss which bakery bakes the best Stollen.
